title: Do You Need a Meta Ads Agency? Ad Spend Thresholds Explained
summary: Hire a Facebook ads agency only when its fee leaves enough media to learn from. Meta budget rules, published agency minimums and a $2,000 budget example.
body_markdown:
You do not need an agency to run Facebook ads, and Meta's minimum budget is small, though Ads Manager does enforce one that varies by country and objective. The real test is whether the agency fee leaves enough media to learn from, and whether the work you are buying, such as weekly video creative, is something your team cannot produce itself. If you do outsource, Knowlify is our top pick for done-for-you video ads on Facebook and Instagram.


Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


The sections below use Meta's own budget rules and the minimums that agencies publish. Where a number is our arithmetic rather than a published figure, we say so.


## Does Meta set a minimum budget for Facebook ads?


Meta's pages answer in two ways. Its[advertising overview](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads) says each ad objective has a recommended daily budget but no minimum budget, and that an ad should run for at least 7 days so the system can learn. Its help center page on[minimum budgets](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/203183363050448) says Meta requires a minimum that varies by country and objective, and that Ads Manager shows an alert when a budget falls below it. In practice, you can start small, but a very small budget may be flagged.


The same help page says that with a cost per result goal, your daily budget should be at least five times that goal. Meta's[ad pricing page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/pricing) suggests starting with at least $5 and spreading the budget over at least seven days. Meta's[learning phase guidance](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/112167992830700) says an ad set usually stops learning after about 50 results in the week following its last significant edit. That number, not a dollar floor, is the constraint that matters for a small account.


Spend can also move around. Meta's[daily budget rules](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/190490051321426) allow up to 75% over a daily budget on a given day, and a $100 daily budget can spend $175 on one day but no more than $700 in a week. Plan for that variation when you set a monthly cap.


## What spend and business-size thresholds do agencies publish?


Published minimums vary widely, and several are stated as a size of business or a media budget rather than a fee. Read each one as the level at which that provider's model is designed to work, and ask whether the minimum applies to the scope you want.


Provider Published threshold Against a $2,000 monthly budget


[Admiral Media](https://admiral.media/ai-ugc-agency/) Ideal clients invest US$50,000 or more a month in paid media; Starter is €10,000 for 20 AI UGC ads Built for far larger media budgets


[AI Vidia](https://ai-vidia.com/pricing) Performance Retainer at €8,500 a month, recommended from €50,000 a month in paid social; a one-time €4,900 pilot The retainer is out of range; the pilot is a one-time test


[Darkroom](https://www.darkroomagency.com/) Homepage: typical fit is consumer brands at $10M to $500M in revenue, poor under roughly $5M.[Services page](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services) : paid media management from $5,000 a month.[Paid media page](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services/paid-media) : from $1,500 a month depending on channels Not built for a small account


[Airpost](https://www.airpost.ai/pricing) From $6,000 a month for a platform and dedicated AI video team Exceeds the budget


[Adside AI](https://www.adside.ai/pricing) Managed service at 10% of ad spend with a $3,500 monthly minimum The minimum exceeds the budget


[KlientBoost](https://www.klientboost.com/services/facebook-ads-agency/) Works with ad budgets from $5,000 a month; also sells a one-time audit or setup Only the one-time audit or setup fits


[LYFE Marketing](https://www.lyfemarketing.com/facebook-advertising-services/) Services from $650 to $2,500 a month, a $300 setup fee, and at least $500 a month in ad spend recommended on top The closest match, with a fee near a third of the media


Knowlify ([Facebook ads service](https://knowlify.com/facebook-ads-agency) ) Custom quote, no public rate card Ask for a scoped proposal first


Darkroom's two monthly figures come from two different pages, and neither page explains the gap, so ask for a written quote that names your channels. The thresholds that matter most are the ones tied to a provider's own model: Admiral and AI Vidia state the media spend they are built for, and Darkroom states a revenue range. A $2,000 account sits well below all three.


## What does a $2,000 monthly budget actually buy?


Start with the arithmetic. A $2,000 month is about $66.67 a day and about $467 a week (our arithmetic, assuming a 30-day month). Meta's five-times rule means a daily budget that size supports a cost per result goal of about $13.33 or lower.


The learning threshold is stricter. To reach about 50 results in a single week from one ad set, a $467 weekly budget needs a cost per result near $9.33 or lower (our arithmetic). If your offer costs more per result than that, the ad set will take longer than a week to leave the learning phase, and an agency fee competes directly with the media that would fund that learning.


The fee side is just as concrete. LYFE Marketing's page says its Facebook services range from $650 to $2,500 a month, with a $300 setup fee that it will waive on request, and it recommends at least $500 a month in ad spend on top. At the low end, a $650 fee on $2,000 of media means about 25% of everything you spend goes to the agency, and about 64% under Adside's $3,500 minimum (our arithmetic: fee divided by fee plus media). Run every quote through that same division before you compare agencies.
